key_insight: DSGNAR is a second-order training framework that makes PINNs far better conditioned, enabling much higher accuracy and faster convergence than standard optimizers.
engineering_relevance: This matters for scientific computing because it brings PINNs closer to classical solver accuracy on difficult PDEs, including nonlinear, chaotic, multi-scale, high-dimensional, and Navier-Stokes problems.
method: Uses a doubly-sketched Gauss-Newton approximation to scale second-order optimization.
Adds adaptive control of both regularization and step length via a ratio-based strategy.
Targets the ill-conditioned PINN loss landscape to stabilize training and improve convergence.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark PDEs, the method achieved errors as low as 3×10^-16 in double precision, improved Burgers’ results by five orders of magnitude, and was up to eight orders better on a high-dimensional Poisson problem while remaining faster.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate implementation of the sketched second-order updates and may still be sensitive to precision, architecture choice, and hyperparameter tuning in practical deployments.
paper_title: An Optimisation Framework for the Well-Conditioned Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
